Man City XI vs Fulham: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Premier League football will soon resume after the international break, with Manchester City hoping to rectify their recent troubles against Fulham in Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.
  • Since suffering their first loss of the Premier League season to Aston Villa, City have fallen to two further defeats at the hands of Brighton and Nottingham Forest.
  • With time to think over the international break, Enzo Maresca has decisions to make when it comes to his starting XI for the visit of Fulham to the Etihad this weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Premier League football will soon resume after the international break, with Manchester City hoping to rectify their recent troubles against Fulham in Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

Since suffering their first loss of the Premier League season to Aston Villa, City have fallen to two further defeats at the hands of Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

With time to think over the international break, Enzo Maresca has decisions to make when it comes to his starting XI for the visit of Fulham to the Etihad this weekend.

He has headaches in defence. Marc Guehi missed international duty with England after coming off with an issue against Nottingham Forest, while he has since confirmed Abdukodir Khusanov and Matheus Nunes are both doubts for the match, too. Antoine Semenyo is a long-term absentee with a knee issue.

In goal, Gianluigi Donnarumma has come under fire for his performances, but it seems unlikely that Maresca would drop the Italian international just yet.

With Guehi and Khusanov doubts, it makes sense to predict a centre-back pairing of Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol. Left back Nico O’Reilly is returning to both form and favour with Maresca, while Nunes may be forced to drop out for Rico Lewis.

Enzo Fernandez is definitely a favourite of Maresca, and while the Argentine travelled to South America to play two friendlies with his national side, he was rested for 35 minutes in the second game.

Elliott Anderson received a similar amount of rest while away with England - coming off early during their 3-2 victory over Spain courtesy of a red card.

City paid over £250million to overhaul their midfield this summer, and the duo’s quality should see them start.

It has been revealed that phil Foden was dropped for the defeat to Forest, but City’s performance might encourage Maresca to restore the England international to the starting XI. In order to fit both Foden and Rayan Cherki into the side, the former will have to go on the right wing, with the latter playing centrally.

We’re predicting that Jeremy Doku will get the nod on the left - with Erling Haaland leading the line up top.

Industry News: Martinez insists Leverkusen must be ‘strong at the back’ against Paderborn

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.
  • Carles Martinez insisted his Bayer Leverkusen side must be "strong at the back" if they are to defeat Paderborn on Saturday.
  • Leverkusen have lost two of their last three Bundesliga matches, but defeated Koln 2-1 before the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Carles Martinez insisted his Bayer Leverkusen side must be "strong at the back" if they are to defeat Paderborn on Saturday.

Leverkusen have lost two of their last three Bundesliga matches, but defeated Koln 2-1 before the international break.

The Werkself lost 4-2 at home to Stuttgart following a 3-0 defeat at Hoffenheim, leaving Leverkusen fifth in the Bundesliga, five points behind Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

Paderborn, meanwhile, are 13th in the league after nine games, three points clear of the relegation playoff places, but also just six points behind Leverkusen.

Paderborn (W1 D3) are one of only three teams, alongside Bayern and Dortmund, to remain unbeaten in their last four Bundesliga matches.

This four-game unbeaten run equals Paderborn's club record in the Bundesliga, previously achieved only in their first four matches in the competition in 2014.

Martinez is wary of the task ahead in Paderborn, but hopes his Leverkusen players will perform in front of their home fans following the international break.

"The changes to the international break schedule are latest for everyone," Martinez mentioned.

It has been revealed that "We've adapted well. After those gruelling weeks, we've used the time to recover and think carefully about exactly where and how we can improve.

"We can't wait to experience that special [home] atmosphere again – we've really missed it.

It has been revealed that "Paderborn are having a good season, have a clear identity and try to dictate the play themselves. That's why we need to be particularly strong at the back. I expect the best from us.".

Sources indicate that GTA AND B04 BOTH BACK IN THE SAME WEEK! https://t.co/3D9mcqauMV.

— Bayer 04 Leverkusen (@bayer04_en) November 20, 2026.

Bayer Leverkusen – Patrik Schick.

Patrik Schick has scored eight goals in the Bundesliga this season, finding the net in all four of his home appearances.

Eight goals after nine Bundesliga matchdays equals the club record for Leverkusen, previously achieved only by Schick himself (2021-22) and Patrick Helmes (2008-09).

The Czech forward has now scored as many league goals on his own as the entire Paderborn team.

Santiago Castaneda is the only Paderborn outfield player to have played every minute in the Bundesliga this season.

The American has also recorded the second-most interceptions in the league (25, Kaishu Sano: 27) and has covered the second-most distance (108.4 km, Hennes Behrens: 109.2 km).

MATCH PREDICTION: BAYER LEVERKUSEN WIN.

Leverkusen have not lost any of their seven previous professional meetings with Paderborn in all competitions (W6 D1), winning each of the last six.

Against no other current Bundesliga side have Leverkusen played as many professional matches without suffering a single defeat.

Leverkusen lost 3-2 away to Elversberg on the opening matchday of the Bundesliga season and could now lose consecutive Bundesliga games against promoted sides for the first time since 2017.

However, the Werkself are unbeaten in their last 10 home Bundesliga matches against promoted teams (W7 D3).

Paderborn are one of three teams without an away win in the Bundesliga this season, alongside Koln and Union Berlin.

Paderborn have drawn three of those matches (L1), including two 0-0 draws, and have conceded only five away goals – only Dortmund have conceded fewer on the road (four).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona have confirmed they have no plans to sell Alejandro Balde and insist the Manchester United-linked left-back remains an ‘important player’ for the club going forward.

Balde has been with Barca since the age of just eight, making a total of 173 appearances in all competitions since breaking into the first-team squad back in 2021.

In that time, the 23-year-old has helped the Catalan giants win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles – the most recent coming under Hansi Flick last season.

However, Balde has become an increasingly peripheral figure at the Camp Nou in recent months, with all five of his appearances this term coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at Barca and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, this has forced Balde to consider his options and the full-back is understood to be keen on joining Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United in January.

Other reports suggest that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender views the Premier League as a possible escape route.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

In a recent development, ‘Obviously, he’s in an uncomfortable situation. The player wants to play.

According to recent reports, ‘He’s one of our own and he’s still an important player. It’s true that he’s not playing right now, although he’s ready if the manager needs him.’.

Deco, Barca’s sporting director, was similarly unequivocal when asked if a transfer deal could be on the cards for Balde.

‘No,’ the ex-Barca, Chelsea and Portugal responded.

‘There is also the player’s side, but he hasn’t told us anything about being unhappy, that’s not the case.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Manchester United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer in order to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, the club’s only specialist in the position other than academy product Harry Amass.

The Red Devils ultimately failed to bolster their full-back options, though, which has come back to bite them already this season, with Shaw sidelined for the last month through injury.

Diogo Dalot was therefore forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back in the bleak final weeks of Michael Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s understood Lewis Hall had been identified as United’s number one left-back target ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, but Newcastle made it clear the England international would not be sold for anything other than an astronomical price.

Hall would go on to put pen to paper on a newly introduced long-term deal at St James’ Park, tying him to the Magpies until 2031.

Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell have also been linked in recent months.

Tottenham are set to welcome back a host of players ahead of their Premier League clash at home to Ipswich this weekend.

Destiny Udogie, Savio, James Maddison, and Lucas Bergvall were all pictured in training at Hotspur Way this week and are now in contention for minutes on Saturday.

Udogie was left out of Roberto De Zerbi’s squad as Spurs lost 1-0 to Leeds before the international break, though the Italian left-back took to social media to suggest he was not injured.

De Zerbi has previously mentioned that Udogie’s injuries were becoming “problematic”, with the 23-year-old starting just two league games this season.

Sources indicate that savio, meanwhile, is in line to return to action for the first time since October’s 1-1 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger has missed Spurs’ last four league games with a muscular issue.

Spurs sorely lacked a creative threat against Leeds. But despite naming Maddison on the bench at Elland Road, De Zerbi didn't bring him on in search of a goal, raising concerns about his fitness.

Maddison has struggled to train consistently since the start of the season and came off midway through Spurs’ 2-0 win over Chelsea with a suspected groin concern.

The 29-year-old has not featured since that historic victory at Stamford Bridge, despite being available for selection. Still, it is hoped that during the international break he has had time to work on building his fitness.

Bergvall is also expected to be in contention for minutes against Ipswich, having returned from a knee injury.

The Swedish midfielder was not called up for international duty by Graham Potter, but could make his first appearance since the start of October after returning to Spurs training.

Mathys Tel is expected to be out for up to three weeks with an Achilles injury sustained following a heavy tackle from Leeds defender Jayden Bogle.

It is also unclear whether reserve goalkeeper Martin Dubravka has recovered from a knee injury, while Tosin Adarabioyo remains out with a calf concern.

Long-term absentee Xavi Simons is ahead of schedule in his recovery from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, but remains some time away from a return to match action.

Wilson Odobert is also out with an ACL injury, while Chelsea loanee Mykhailo Mudryk is still missing with an ankle ligament injury that has kept him out since September.

  • The Argentine has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the Red Devils, but is out of contract at the end of the season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona have Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez on their transfer shortlist ahead of the January window, according to reports.

Martinez is into his fifth season at United after signing from Ajax for £57million in 2022.

The Argentine has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the Red Devils, but is out of contract at the end of the season.

United do have the option to trigger a 12-month extension to Martinez’s contract, but they may have reservations after he launched a scathing public critique of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

And now, Mundo Deportivo reports that Barcelona could be waiting in the wings to pounce as they seek to add a centre-back in the January window.

Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni and Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck are also being considered by the Catalalan giants as options to strengthen Hansi Flick’s side.

But Martinez is viewed as the ‘most economical’ alternative, with the Barca keen on his experience and capability to operate on the left side of defence.

The report adds that Martinez would be willing to listen to an offer, although the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as United’s fresh manager could complicate Barcelona’s pursuit.

Pochettino will take charge of his first match against Liverpool on Sunday, but former Red Devils defender Gary Neville expects Martinez will be one of several defenders to make way in the coming transfer windows.

Sources indicate that ‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Scott has established himself as one of the most sought-after central midfielders in English football having joined Bournemouth from Bristol City back in 2023.
  • With attentions beginning to turn towards the January transfer window, speculation is mounting that the 23-year-old could have his head turned amid strong interest from the Premier League’s elite.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frank Lampard appears to have endorsed Chelsea’s pursuit of Alex Scott while revealing his ‘love’ for the ‘quality’ Bournemouth and England midfielder.

Scott has established himself as one of the most sought-after central midfielders in English football having joined Bournemouth from Bristol City back in 2023.

With attentions beginning to turn towards the January transfer window, speculation is mounting that the 23-year-old could have his head turned amid strong interest from the Premier League’s elite.

Though he picked up a thigh injury while on international duty with England last month, Scott’s outstanding performance in the Three Lions’ thumping 7-0 win over Croatia did little to quieten rumours of a potential major-money move.

Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham have all been credited with an interest in recent weeks and months, but Chelsea reportedly find themselves in pole position to land Scott this winter.

The Blues are actively scouring the market for midfield reinforcements after failing to bring in a replacement for Enzo Fernandez in the summer and are said to be ‘increasingly confident’ of reaching an agreement for Scott.

Up until this point, Bournemouth have publicly played down speculation that Scott could be on the move, especially midway through the campaign when they risk derailing the side’s encouraging progress under Marco Rose.

However, it’s understood an offer in region of £100million could be enough to convince the Cherries into selling Scott in what would undoubtedly be one of this January’s biggest deals.

One man who knows more than anyone what it takes to thrive in Chelsea’s midfield is Lampard, arguably the club’s greatest ever player, who won 14 trophies across an illustrious 13-year career at Stamford Bridge.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

During a wide-ranging interview on the Rio Ferdinand Presents YouTube channel, Lampard made it clear just how highly he rated Scott when he was asked to name his dream Premier League midfield three on current form.

‘I don’t want to leave anyone out because there are some teams that are doing some stuff… I’m loving what Brighton are doing at the moment but you do come back to the bigger players sometimes, maybe Cole Palmer or Rayan Cherki,’ the Coventry head coach told Ferdinand.

‘I love Alex Scott at Bournemouth, I think he’s quality.

‘He’s injured now for a short period but I think he’s real quality in that modern all-rounder [role], in the double six/eight.’.

Revealing other candidates for his midfield three, Lampard added: ‘I’ve got to put Elliot Anderson in there, in my opinion, for the way he’s playing.

‘I’m trying to think of the attacking options… I think I’d put Anderson and Declan Rice as the two sixes and then I’ll go for an eight/ten.

‘I’m trying to think of the eight-ten that’s really being decisive at the minute. Rayan Cherki is doing bits, I love Cole Palmer.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Lampard went on to express his admiration for Martin Odegaard, explaining how he had shut down one of his close friends who had been criticising the Arsenal captain.

It has been revealed that ‘I really like Martin Odegaard. A mate of mine, an Arsenal fan, doesn’t like Odegaard, he gets on my nerves! He’s a good player,’ he went on.

It has been revealed that ‘He [Odegaard] brilliant. I bumped into him with my son as well recently, him and Kai Havertz, I know Kai, at a hotel, my boy was buzzing and they were so lovely with my boy, not that that makes them good players.

‘They were brilliant, the pair of them. And I said to my son, “This boy [Odegaard] is a good player”, because you see all sides of the game, especially when you do my job and you watch him press and what he does for the team.’.

Lampard also praised Odegaard’s midfield partner Rice and questioned the ‘harsh’ criticism the England international has at times received during his career.

‘I do love Declan Rice and I think he’s become a conversation point because when you get to be so good and compete at such a level, people try to pick holes in your game and I think it’s harsh,’ he continued.

‘I think he’s a really good player and it’s just a common thing that comes with the territory.

‘It’s fine and Declan will just shrug it off.’.

Mauricio Pochettino will pick his first Manchester United team on Sunday for a daunting debut away at Liverpool.

The Argentine was appointed Michael Carrick’s successor last week and only arrived in the north-west on Wednesday, leaving him just a handful of sessions to prepare his side for a crunch fixture.

As such, wholesale changes from life under Carrick are not forecast, at least in terms of setup. After all, both managers have a penchant for the same 4-2-3-1 formation.

Carlos Baleba remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained against Roma in the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko also out until the new year, but Pochettino may well be boosted by the returns of Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw. The latter seems the more likely of the two, with Rashford yet to be pictured in training since the international break.

Pochettino is known to be very fond of Rashford, and has reportedly attempted to sign him to other teams he has managed, meaning he can expect to get the nod if fit.

Sources indicate that should fit-again Shaw slot in at left-back, he may do so as one of two fresh faces in the back four. Lisandro Martinez has served his red card suspension and will be available to partner Harry Maguire, with Diogo Dalot at right-back.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo will sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

It has been revealed that patrick Dorgu is expected to be fit, too, but it remains to be seen whether he can unseat Matheus Cunha off the left. He could also deputise Shaw if his fitness levels are not up to par.

Leaked drone footage of United’s Thursday training session appeared to show Pochettino working on tactics with a tight-knit group of ten outfield players, leading some to speculate that he might be dealing with Sunday’s starters. The presence of Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass in the group rather debunks this, though, given neither has started a Premier League match this season.

Predicted Man Utd XI vs Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo.

Time and date: 4.30pm GMT on Sunday, November 22.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026.

After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.

It has been revealed that and what a weekend we have coming up. Old gaffers in upcoming colours, fierce rivalries and some seminal fixtures in the context of the whole season.

With so much to look forward to this weekend, Daily Mail Sport looks over the key reasons to be excited for the return of the world's most electric league.

After a flying start to the campaign Manchester City have begun to run into serious problems under Enzo Maresca and have lost their last three Premier League games on the trot.

And after a particularly humiliating defeat away to Nottingham Forest, who hadn't scored at home before the Cityzens' visit, Maresca and his squad will be desperate for three points especially with champions Arsenal now six points clear.

City have a good opportunity to turn things around, though, as they host a Fulham side who have endured a terrible run of form against Saturday’s opponents. In fact, the Cottagers have failed to beat City in their last 20 Premier League meetings - a run stretching back 14 years.

But, as ever in the Premier League, nothing is guaranteed and Alvaro Arbeloa’s side are showing promising signs - having enjoyed an unbeaten run in their past four games.

Enzo Maresca's side started in scintillating form but have lost their last three games.

Bonfire night has only just passed but don’t be surprised to see fireworks in west London on Saturday as old rivals Chelsea and Leeds do battle at Stamford Bridge.

Recent findings suggest that after comfortably surviving in their returning year last season, Leeds have kicked on and have quietly emerged as a strong contender for European football. Daniel Farke’s side currently sit ninth, just two points off fifth place Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that the Blues on the other hand have endured a stuttering, frustrating start to the season. Xabi Alonso’s heralded front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have showcased their terrifying attacking prowess, but the Blues boss’ mystifying tinkering, plus inconsistent performances, has seen his side drop points against Spurs and Sunderland.

However, form will go out of the window as this rivalry - 55 years in the making - is reignited.

Chelsea will be hoping for a repeat of their 6-3 win over Leeds in the league cup this season but Daniel Farke's men will not be as easy to get past in the league.

After Pierre Sage’s dismal start to life in south London, the Crystal Palace board did not hang around and gave the Frenchman the boot after just five months in charge.

And the Eagles have made sure to replace him with someone who has Premier League pedigree, Thomas Frank.

Now while recent memories of the Danish gaffer are almost universally negative it is easy to forget that before his calamitous stint at Tottenham he worked wonders down in west London for Brentford.

Sources indicate that and he has every chance of doing the same at Selhurst Park. The job will be far from easy as his fresh team presently sit rock bottom of the league, but considering Frank’s high pressing and wide set playstyle, Palace’s squad looks a good fit for the Dane.

His first game back will be a tough test, away to Frank Lampard’s resurgent Coventry, but Frank - and the travelling Palace contingent - will be hoping for a fresh manager bounce in the east Midlands.

Thomas Frank returns to London to take charge of a struggling Crystal Palace side.

With City faltering and Liverpool and Chelsea failing to hit their stride, the Premier League title race is fast developing into a one-horse competition - and Mikel Arteta will not care one bit.

The Spaniard’s well-oiled machine looks near impossible to stop but as Brighton proved before the last international break, they are not infallible and are set for a tough test returning from the latest break.

The Gunners travel to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle in what promises to be another thriller.

In years past the trip up north has proved to be a banana skin for Arsenal and Arteta, losing four out of their last six games there.

In a recent development, however, Newcastle fans fear their side are fast becoming a fading force and the trip to the North East isn’t perhaps as intimidating as it once was. After all, the Gunners picked up a stoppage time win there last season on their way to the title.

Mikel Arteta's side are hitting their stride but face a tough test at St James' Park.

The surprise package of the season has undoubtedly been Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls who are perched in second place after 10 excellent games.

According to recent reports, they remain the only side to have beaten the champions Arsenal and are the league’s top scorers by five goals. They are efficient, fun to watch and have scored a plethora of absolute scorchers this season, but the question on everyone’s lips is: can they keep it up?

History would suggest that overperforming teams tend to settle into the pack after a fast start, and end up battling it out for a coveted spot in a lesser European competition.

In a recent development, but somehow this year it feels different. Brighton appear to have everything they might need to maintain this form and seriously challenge for a Champions League place.

The squad has depth and dynamism with a littany of players boasting youthful exuberance, sprinkled with the experience of the ever-reliable Lewis Dunk and the resurgent Pascal Gross. Crucially, they have a top, motivated manager hellbent on breaking the mould.

Upon return from the break Brighton travel a stubborn Hull side, for their first ever top flight meeting between the two sides.

Brighton have been truly sensational in the opening ten games but can they keep this up going into the notoriously tough winter period.

It seems that after nearly 18 months at Liverpool Florian Wirtz is finally beginning to perform.

After a dismal first year in England in which he only registered nine goals and assists in 33 Premier League games the £116million man is starting to rediscover the form that earned him that valuation.

He enjoyed possibly his best performance in a red shirt just before the break, scoring and assisting in a 3-1 away win against Crystal Palace, and has taken that form into his international performances.

The attacking midfielder got one against Serbia in a routine 3-1 win as well as netting a brace in a 5-0 drubbing of the Netherlands - with one of his strikes an absolute pearler.

The Kop will hope this is the precursor to Wirtz seriously hitting form in the Premier League but the 23-year-old still has a lot to do before he repays the money Liverpool paid for him last year.

Florian Wirtz looks in the mood after a couple of excellent performances for Germany under ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

There is no skirting around the biggest story of the international break - the psychodrama at Manchester United. The two-week break saw the Red Devils wave goodbye to Michael Carrick and say hello to Mauricio Pochettino, hoping the incoming Argentinian will inspire a much-needed turnaround.

After an emotional press conference in which he said goodbye to the US men’s national team, who he has managed for the last two years, the former Spurs and Chelsea boss is tasked with getting his fresh club out of the relegation places and finding some much-needed stability.

And it will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, who takes his strugglers to the Anfield cauldron on Sunday, to face a Liverpool side who will have to travel to Anfield, to face a Liverpool side already 10 points ahead.

Factor in the history and rivalry this fixture holds and we are in for a cracker on Merseyside. The smart money would be on Liverpool but as we have seen so many times before a new manager bounce can transform a team in a matter of hours.

And that is all he will have to prepare his charges for their trip to Liverpool - with the new boss landing in Manchester on Wednesday morning to begin work straightaway. Welcome back, Pochettino.

Poch is back and this time in red but he will have his work cut out for him managing a dysfunctional United side presently sat in 18th.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wes Brown believes Manchester United should still be aiming for a top-five finish this season after Mauricio Pochettino was appointed head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has officially taken the reins at Old Trafford after his final two matches with the United States national team.

Pochettino has undoubtedly been thrown in at the deep end, with United winless in their last eight Premier League matches and facing Liverpool in his first game on Sunday.

But former Red Devils defender Brown believes that the Argentine has the quality to inspire a quick turnaround from his new crop of players.

In a recent development, ‘Poch is very experienced, and he has his own style of play, but it’s all about consistency, he told Metro. ‘Making the players believe they’re good enough and making sure they do it week in, week out.

‘We’ve had no momentum; we’ve played well here and there in games, and when we did we managed to score, but at the same time we’ve been very poor at times and open to teams scoring at will, making loads of mistakes.

‘The confidence isn’t there, but he’ll be coming in and just trying to get consistency through the team.

‘When a latest manager comes in, the players really make an effort, that’s just the way it goes, but then it’s up to the manager to keep that going through the season, and whether or not he’ll be able to, we’ll all have to see.’.

Pochettino brings with him extensive experience in the Premier League but also a proven track record of nurturing young talent into the first team.

And Brown is hopeful that academy duo Shea Lacey and Harry Amass could benefit from the Argentine’s arrival, adding: ‘If anyone, you think those two might come in and get a game under the latest manager to show what they can do.

In a recent development, ‘I think at the moment, you are looking at Shea Lacey and thinking, “Yeah, he can get a game”. He delivers, he runs, he works hard.

Pochettino faces a trip to Anfield for his first game in charge (Picture: Getty).

In a recent development, ‘But I also think when you’re in a position where you don’t necessarily just bring in the young lads as well. I think that’s a tough gig if I’m being honest, and you can’t just bring them in when the team’s like this.’.

Pochettino will have to endure a frenetic start to life in the United dugout, with a run of eight games in 21 days starting at Anfield on Sunday.

But with plenty of the season still ahead, Brown thinks United should still be aiming high if they can start fast under their eighth permanent boss since Alex Ferguson’s retirement.

‘There’s still a chance of getting into Europe, 100 per cent,’ Brown added, speaking to Metro ahead of the year’s second Counter-Strike Major.

It has been revealed that ‘Even though it’s been very disappointing, even if you look at the table now, the gap is not that substantial. It’s maybe 8-9 points from a European place, if that.

In a recent development, ‘So you’ve still got to have that in the back of your mind. It’s Manchester United; that’s where you aim to be, if not higher, and I’m sure Poch will definitely be looking to get us in that sort of area and going in that direction.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that crystal Palace sacked Pierre Sage and hired Thomas Frank because they needed change. They need more than their fresh manager seems to realise.

The Dane revealed on Thursday that the 3-4-3 formation Palace have become so used to playing under Oliver Glasner and then briefly under Sage will “definitely be one of our systems, a go-to - and then we'll see what we change.”.

The truth, though, is that while flexibility is good, the formation is one of the things that does need a rethink.

Frank was right about one thing, at least. “It is obvious that this squad is recruited to 3-4-3”, he mentioned. “That's why we have very good players in their positions.”.

But those “very good players” are not still at Selhurst Park. The Eagles have been persevering with a system that suits players no longer at the club, something the upcoming boss must put right.

Wind the clock back less than a year and after a 2-1 win over London rivals Fulham, Palace sat fourth in the Premier League table in a season destined produce historic European silverware.

In a recent development, adam Wharton was firing. Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta were doing well to cover up the loss of Eberechi Eze to Arsenal. Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi were two-thirds of one of the finest centre-back crews in the division. Daniel Munoz was the most enjoyable high-flying wing-back to watch in England. In charge was Glasner, a man who knew exactly how to eke out the best of Palace’s 3-4-3. Life could not get any better.

Now, it is an entirely different landscape.

Though Jaydee Canvot and Chelsea-bound Honest Ahanor are promising players, Palace also have Axel Disasi - who still has a mistake in him - and there is therefore an awful lot of pressure on the shoulders of the one central defender who lived through all the good times: Chris Richards.

According to recent reports, in their last game, midfielder Jefferson Lerma started there while actual centre-backs sat on the bench: which is never a good sign. A 3-4-3 system involves playing one more centre-half than most teams, and yet for Palace that means one more player in a position where the quality just isn’t there anymore since Guehi and Lacroix’s departures.

Industry observers note that in midfield, Wharton has lost his way this season and is being overrun alongside Daichi Kamada. Switching to a 4-2-3-1 - a formation Frank knows well - would allow three midfielders to get a better handle on things, provided the No10 adopted defensive responsibilities. The likelihood of such a porous Palace midfield would drop.

In a recent development, at wing-back, only Anan Khalaili suits a back five any more than a back four. Oscar Mingueza is the more defensively astute right-back. The pair should share game time depending on whether Palace are hunting a leveller or preserving a lead. On the other flank, Tyrick Mitchell has a claim to being the best one-v-one defender in the Premier League. Scaling him from wing-back to left-back would be no matter.

Recent findings suggest that palace must remember where they are. They sit bottom of the Premier League by a point and have the worst defence in the division.

Frank has been hired to save them, with plenty of time to do so. That means plenty of time to find a way of getting the best out of the squad as it is now, with the players available. Not getting the best out of a team that no longer exists.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andriy Shevchenko has demanded an apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk after he blamed Ukraine’s national team for his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old initially faced a four-year ban but returned to football this summer after he accepted that he had breached anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension equal to the time he had already served.

Speaking to YouTube channel Guest of Gordon this week, Mudryk was asked who he felt was to blame for the adverse finding.

‘The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team,’ Mudryk said.

It has been revealed that ‘It should never have existed. I probably haven’t mentioned it publicly yet but I’m saying it now.

‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.’.

Sources indicate that asked how meldonium got into his system, Mudryuk mentioned: ‘The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

‘There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.’.

Former Chelsea striker Shevchenko, who is now the president of the Ukrainian Association of Football, has hit back at Mudryk’s claims and has described the winger’s version of events as ‘baseless slander’.

In a recent development, ‘I want to express my position on the accusations of Mykhailo Mudryk. Loud statements were made about the UAF, the Ukrainian national team. This is a baseless slander against our people, who do their job honestly and professionally,’ Shevchenko stated in a statement to Tribuna Ukraine.

‘Instead, after the suspension of Mykhailo Mudryk, his representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to artificially find an employee who would take responsibility for the appearance of meldonium in his doping sample.

‘The UAF refused – such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work. The accusations from Mykhailo’s representatives were not confirmed or proven after many studies and inspections. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English association confirm this.

According to recent reports, ‘After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during the national team training camp. The team staff complied with this request.

‘Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also agreed for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him during the training camp. These people monitored his regimen and recovery and helped him with his daily life.

It has been revealed that ‘The UAF has completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested and have been in contact with those who worked on the case.

‘I know people who have been working in the national team for many years. I trust them, because during all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make one doubt their professionalism.

Industry observers note that ‘If Mykhailo has evidence to support his words, let him provide it. If there is no such evidence, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he questioned.’.

Manchester United are considering a move for Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic in the January transfer window, according to reports.

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at United this week having replaced Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the international break.

But the Argentine begins his tenure at Old Trafford without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

United have made funds available to strengthen Pochettino’s squad in January and the club are targeting a new striker.

According to The i Paper, Matanovic is on United’s striker shortlist alongside Folarin Balogun, who Monaco are open to selling in the January transfer window.

The report adds that United are also looking to bolster Pochettino’s defence with Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey and left-back Antonee Robinson under consideration.

Matanovic, meanwhile, was signed by Freiburg in an €8 million (£6.8m) deal from Eintracht Frankfurt last year.

The Croatia international, who offers a physical presence in attack at 6ft 5in, has scored 23 goals in 64 games for Freiburg so far.

At international level, Matanovic has scored two goals in 17 appearances for Croatia and came off the bench in three games at the World Cup in the summer.

When asked about his future in September, Matanovic insisted he had not received an approach to leave Freiburg.

‘As for me, I’m right now in Freiburg. There has been absolutely no contact with anyone from my side,’ the striker stated.

Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley have both returned to Liverpool training, with potential for them both to return within weeks.

Bradley has been sidelined since suffering a serious knee injury against Arsenal back in January.

Leoni, meanwhile, was a victim of profoundly bad luck when he tore his ACL on his debut for the Reds in September 2025, just weeks after signing from Parma.

But after months of rehabilitation, Iraola has confirmed that both men resumed training with the Liverpool first team during the November international break and could soon be in contention for competitive play.

“Very good news from both sides,” Iraola confirmed on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that “I think the international break was the best moment for us to try to introduce them slowly, slowly with the rest of the players. They have done this and now even in the last part of the week they have already started doing things with the team.

“Obviously they are still not available but it’s very good news that they are able to do things with the group.”.

He continued, adding that Liverpool would be gentle with the pair’s reintegration as they look to avoid setbacks.

“It’s true that they have to be loaded carefully – they don’t train every day with us. One day, yes. The next day, not. The next day, yes. We are in the last part of this process, a long process.

“But both of them are looking good and I hope they can play in some weeks.”.

It is said Bradley and Leoni have become close friends as they went through their rehabilitation together at Liverpool’s Kirkby training ground.

Iraola also confirmed Jeremie Frimpong, Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai are all in line to play a role as Liverpool host Manchester United on Sunday.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has addressed what has been a difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign for the 20-time English champions.
  • The Red Devils are presently down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, boasting just eight points from their opening 10 matches of the campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 15:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:01.

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has addressed what has been a difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign for the 20-time English champions.

The Red Devils are presently down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, boasting just eight points from their opening 10 matches of the campaign.

The decision was made to sack Michael Carrick earlier this month, with Mauricio Pochettino coming in as his replacement.

Berrada has now explained the reasoning behind Carrick's dismissal and the arrival of Pochettino, who will lead Man United into Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool.

Industry observers note that when asked whether he was confident Man United are moving in the right direction, Berrada told Sky Sports News: "One hundred per cent. I know it's difficult to say this when you're sitting 18th in the Premier League table.

"It's clear - it's not good enough, not acceptable, and that's why we've made the change that we've made, so that we can move forward.

"But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. The foundations are there. I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction.".

When asked about Carrick's dismissal, Berrada stated: "It was a very difficult decision, to be honest, especially given all the affection everyone at the club has for Michael.

Sources indicate that "When he took over the team last season, they did very well under him. They were playing some really good football, winning important matches. We qualified for the Champions League and finished third.

"We felt at the time he'd earned the right to continue leading the team. So when we started the season, it's clearly been a lot more difficult than we expected. The results haven't been good enough. I think we've dropped off in many areas.

"We wanted to give ourselves until the November international break to really take stock of what was happening with the team, what were the areas that needed to be improved. And in the end, we took the decision to make a change of coach.

Sources indicate that "Unfortunately, sometimes when you're in the middle of the season, that's the one decision that you can make that can provoke a reaction, that can provoke a change in the dynamic. So that's why we had to take the decision.".

On Pochettino, Berrada stated: "He has a tremendous amount of passion and energy. We see it already in the two days he's been with us.

According to recent reports, "There's a buzz about the place, and he's brought that with his staff. He has a very clear philosophy, identity of how he wants to see the team play. And I think he's coming just at the right time for him and us to be able to help the team and take us forward.

"He's equally as ambitious as we are, which is: we want to win titles.

"You have to think that when you're playing for Manchester United, when the results aren't going well, the pressure and the scrutiny is enormous. And all that noise around the club and around the players can be difficult to manage.

"So I think in Mauricio we bring somebody that has just the right amount of maturity and experience at the big clubs to be able to put his arms around the players and to let them perform at their highest potential.".

Man United will be aiming to post just their second Premier League win of the season when they head to Liverpool on Sunday afternoon to tackle Liverpool.

Latest Update: The Premier League’s newest managers have a lot to lose

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank respectively, Manchester United and Crystal Palace have gone for a pair of managers whose reputations in English football could do with a good start this weekend to avoid the varying levels of doom that have surrounded Old Trafford and Selhurst Park from peaking again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Farewell then, Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage, who have gone off to the great significant Premier League managerial scrapheap in the sky after an international break where only the identity of the next James Bond could rival speculation over Carrick’s eventual replacement in particular.

In Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank respectively, Manchester United and Crystal Palace have gone for a pair of managers whose reputations in English football could do with a good start this weekend to avoid the varying levels of doom that have surrounded Old Trafford and Selhurst Park from peaking again.

It’s a good thing, then, that despite their contrasting styles, both are known for putting emphasis on energy – not just in how their team plays on the pitch, but in how the culture around the club feels off it.

In a recent development, pochettino has made headlines before for his love of lemons (they absorb negative energy, he’ll have you know) and his apparent sixth sense. In his 2017 book Brave New World, he wrote: ‘What most influences my decisions is my ability to see if the right energy is flowing.’.

What kind of energy he felt flowing through director of football Jason Wilcox is anyone’s guess at this stage, but his emphasis on things like togetherness and the mindset of his players could finally be the key to starting to turn the Suez canal tanker that United have become, on the pitch at least.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If Pochettino comes across as part high-level manager, part yoga teacher, then Frank has the air of an executive ready to rebuild the culture at an ailing business.

A year off from football was on the cards after he was sacked by Tottenham in February. The Dane turned down Palace during the summer in favour of World Cup punditry and attending the Tour de France, and didn’t sound completely convinced he’d made the right decision to cut that break short.

Industry observers note that ‘I was a little bit, “When do I want to go back in? Is it now?” Then this opportunity came up,’ he told PalaceTV this week. ‘I was thinking, this is probably too good to turn down. When I’m sitting here, walking around the training ground, it was just, “Okay, you’re back”, which scared me a little bit, but it’s good.’ Consider the troops rallied.

Questions surround the suitability of both appointments, as Pochettino’s biggest success at Spurs was built on the back of a young, mobile team with something to prove and Frank’s at Brentford came as part of a well-oiled machine. You’d be waiting a long time for anyone to describe United or Palace as either of those these days.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

There’s hope to be found too, for those willing to look for it. Frank did only really have half a bad season and the perceived wisdom is that his personality will suit a ‘smaller’ club – as long as he stays away from any Brighton-branded coffee cups – while of all the managers tasked with fixing United, Pochettino does have the air of a man who can become a messianic figure.

Managerial reputations can only survive a certain number of kicks before there’s no coming back and there may not be many chances left for either man at this level if things go pear-shaped.

However, with both teams playing pretty much every three days for the next month, there are plenty of opportunities for their latest managers to shift the vibes back towards a positive setting.

And even if the wins don’t start flowing, transfer enthusiasts should have something to cling on to as Palace and United are reportedly ready to back their newly introduced men with some signings once the January window opens.

It’s nice to have something to look forward to after Christmas, at least.

Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

📅 10 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
  • By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.
  • Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

It has been revealed that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It has been revealed that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Recent findings suggest that equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Industry observers note that carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

It has been revealed that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

According to recent reports, “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

Sources indicate that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have been dealt a blow in their pursuit of Nico Paz as Real Madrid intend to activate their €80 million (£67m) buyback clause to sign the midfielder from Como, according to reports in Spain.
  • Paz joined Como from Madrid two years ago and has established himself as the talisman in Cesc Fabregas’ side.
  • So far this season, the 22-year-old has been one of the standout performers in the Champions League, scoring three goals and registering five assists in four games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have been dealt a blow in their pursuit of Nico Paz as Real Madrid intend to activate their €80 million (£67m) buyback clause to sign the midfielder from Como, according to reports in Spain.

Paz joined Como from Madrid two years ago and has established himself as the talisman in Cesc Fabregas’ side.

So far this season, the 22-year-old has been one of the standout performers in the Champions League, scoring three goals and registering five assists in four games.

That included a man-of-the-match display in Como’s 4-1 win over United last month while piled more pressure on Michael Carrick.

Last week, reports claimed that United had identified Paz as a potential successor to Bruno Fernandes and were considering a move for the Argentina international next summer.

However, Cadena SER reports that Madrid are ‘determined’ to re-sign Paz at the end of the season and are planning to trigger the €80m (£67m) buyback clause which is part of their agreement with Como.

Madrid had the option to re-sign Paz this year but the midfielder personally requested to stay at Como for another season.

‘I thought this was where I would grow the most. I think I made the right decision and I’m happy I did,’ Paz said in September.

Como spent €60m (£51.77m) on their deal to keep Paz at the club but Madrid, crucially, insisted that a buyout clause would remain part of their agreement.

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has confirmed the club is in active negotiations with Bruno Fernandes over a new contract.

He also admitted United did “absolutely everything” to attempt to convince JJ Gabriel to stay at the club.

United captain Fernandes’ current contract expires at the end of this season, and it has been reported that he has already rejected two offers of a newly introduced deal.

Sources indicate that as the club has struggled in recent years, Fernandes has regularly been able to nick results with inspiring performances. Last season alone, he was responsible for nine goals and 21 assists in the Premier League.

As such, Berrada is desperate to tie him down to a upcoming deal, but kept his cards close to his chest when discussing a potential new contract.

It has been revealed that speaking in a rare interview with Sky Sports, he stated: “We have a tremendous amount of respect for Bruno. We're very fortunate to have him as a captain.

“What he's done for this team over the last six, seven years is absolutely incredible. Last year he won, I think, all the individual awards you can win.

According to recent reports, “And we're very proud to have him as captain. It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private. I think it's something that needs to be discussed behind the scenes between him and the club.”.

One player United have failed to convince to stay, meanwhile, is JJ Gabriel. The 16-year-old winger is widely considered to be one of the game’s brightest talents, but left United stunned earlier this year when he lodged a surprise transfer request.

He has since signed with a newly introduced agency and stated his goodbyes to United, with Real Madrid expected to win the race to take him on. Gabriel will leave United without having made a first-team appearance.

Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4.
  • In a recent development, unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4.
  • In a recent development, the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7,8,9,10,11,12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

In a recent development, unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4. Depending on the relative weight of those energy terms, many different phenomena have been observed: the Hofstadter butterfly depending mainly on the van der Waals coupling13,14,15, commensurate–incommensurate phase transitions driven by van der Waals–strain competition5,6 and flat-band formation that probably involves all three contributions and facilitates superconductivity and correlated insulating phase 16,17,18.

In a recent development, the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies. Varying their relative contributions can switch the system between different atomic arrangements, resulting in structural phase transitions potentially accompanied by the emergence of new electronic phases. This points to a rich underlying phase diagram. Yet experimental platforms that allow controlled exploration of this phase space so far have been lacking.

Here we demonstrate that, by careful tuning of the balance between these competing interactions in a three-layer van der Waals heterostructure, we can reach simultaneous structural and electronic phase transitions, controlled through layer charging, magnetic field or temperature variation. We engineer these transitions in a heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hBN and mhBN on either side: mhBN/graphene/hBN. In such heterostructures, strain is greatly enhanced because mhBN, unlike its bulk counterpart, is free to contract and corrugate (the strain amplitude is controlled by the number of hBN layers), leading to strongly enhanced surface reconstruction19,20,21. The van der Waals interaction of this system is likewise enhanced by the double alignment and can be tuned by gate-charging the graphene layer.

In such heterostructure devices, the structural phase transition reveals itself through an abrupt, global and reversible switch of the stacking configuration, which entails a change of symmetry (analogous to the Bernal-to-rhombohedral transition in graphite22,23,24,25) and results in distinct reconstruction modes observed directly by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). It is accompanied by a unique electronic phase transition: switching between p-doping and n-doping of graphene. Unlike conventional doping, the doping levels before and after the phase transition are discrete rather than continuous in nature, always taking an integer or ‘quantized’ value corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons per moiré unit cell, which we hereafter term integer doping. We attribute this integer doping to electrons (holes) being trapped in the strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (PLLs), formed by the strong moiré surface reconstruction; these localized states constitute flat bands in k-space, as predicted theoretically7,8,9,10,11 and confirmed by STM measurements12. The structural transition alters the atomic arrangement, modifying both the strain and scalar-potential landscapes. In reciprocal space, we interpret this as switching the hybridization of these flat bands between the valence band (AB phase) and the conduction band (AA phase), inverting the sign of the integer doping.

Our heterostructure consists of monolayer graphene that is double-aligned, on one side to hBN and on the other side to mhBN (refs. 19,20). Unlike single alignment, such double-aligned ‘sandwich’ heterostructures can exhibit either parallel or antiparallel orientations corresponding to the 0° and 180° angle alignment between the top and bottom hBN (refs. 2,19,26). The results obtained on both types of device are similar, so in the main text, we focus on the parallel orientation, presenting the analysis for the antiparallel orientation in Supplementary Information Sections 20, 23, 26 and 28 (Supplementary Figs. 30, 41 and 42).

Sources indicate that for either orientation, two energetically competing stacking configurations exist (Fig. 1c,d), which are interconvertible by sliding the mhBN by one interatomic distance relative to the bulk hBN (detailed explanation and simple schematics in Supplementary Information Section 21; Supplementary Figs. 31 and 32). This is analogous to the transition between ABC (rhombohedral) and ABA (Bernal) trilayer graphene, in which a small shift of one of the layers leads to strong reconfigurations of the electronic bands22,23,24,25.

Unlike previous studies that apply a mechanical tool such as an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope tip to locally ‘iron’ the sample to toggle the stacking configurations in confined regions of sample27,28, our system allows global, reversible switching between the two stacking states simply by tuning external parameters, including carrier density n, magnetic field B or temperature T. Such all-electronic control is far better suited to device integration and to triggering new phenomena in transport measurements. The schematic in Fig. 1a illustrates the full phase diagram defined by these external parameters and the intrinsic stacking order, in which the two local minima correspond to the competing AB and AA stacking configurations. Accompanying this switch, the moiré-induced strain distribution and thus the lattice reconstruction changes from triangular to hexagonal patterns (Fig. 1e–h; see also the STM images in Fig. 5a,b), ultimately leading to different pseudomagnetic field (PMF) distributions2,29 (Fig. 5e,f) and different band reconfigurations (Fig. 5g–j).

Sources indicate that we emphasize that the mhBN is essential for enhancing such lattice reconstruction of graphene, as mhBN itself can accommodate a finite amount of strain, allowing both layers (mhBN and graphene) to undergo very strong relaxation. The molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, comparing mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1g,h) and hBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1e,f) heterostructures, clearly demonstrate that the presence of mhBN greatly amplifies the periodic strain induced by moiré reconstruction. The experimental evidence, including room-temperature atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurement of the corrugation (Fig. 1b) and the same measurement with varying hBN layer numbers (1–4 layers; Supplementary Information Section 13; Supplementary Fig. 19) and their corresponding transport properties, is presented in Supplementary Information Section 4. As well as mhBN, alignment also markedly influences the strain, as shown by the calculated corrugation with respect to the twist angle in Fig. 1i.

Two types of transport device are discussed in the main text: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN (Fig. 2a) and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 2b). In the former, the mhBN–hBN interface is intentionally misaligned by 15° to achieve superlubricity, preserving the double-aligned sandwich structure. The two architectures are complementary: the dual-gated capped devices enable higher carrier concentrations and allow the roles of doping and the displacement field to be disentangled (Supplementary Information Section 8), whereas the non-capped mhBN/graphene/hBN structure develops stronger reconstruction, in particular the out-of-plane corrugation at the graphene–mhBN interface (Supplementary Information Section 30).

In a recent development, for both architectures, double alignment of graphene to the hBN crystals on both sides was confirmed by AFM, Raman and transport measurements (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 2). We emphasize that both the double alignment and the presence of mhBN are crucial for the effects we observe, as corroborated by seven types of reference device, none of which exhibit the transition (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4; Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

First, let us examine the initial-state transfer curves (blue) of the two device types in Fig. 2c,d. In the hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN sample, the neutrality point of graphene remains at zero doping, whereas the mhBN/graphene/hBN structure exhibits p-doping. Notably, this p-doping level closely approximates 2n0 (n0 corresponds to doping of one charge carrier per moiré plaquette). In 8 of 9 unencapsulated mhBN/graphene/hBN devices (blue dots in Fig. 2f), the p-doping is quantized at Nn0 (N is an integer between 1 and 4), growing with the moiré period but always fixed at integer multiples of n0.

It has been revealed that in Fig. 2e,f, the moiré period, determined from the carrier density of secondary Dirac points, exceeds in many samples the rigid-lattice limit of 14 nm (set by the 1.8% graphene–hBN lattice mismatch) and even reaches 17.7 nm, a consequence of the strain enhancement by mhBN and double alignment19,20 (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4).

By applying a large positive gate voltage above a certain threshold, a phase transition can be initiated: the moiré period remains unchanged but the samples become n-doped, again by an integer number of electrons per moiré plaquette, for both bottom-gated and dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c,d), and consistently across samples with different moiré sizes (Fig. 2e,f; Supplementary Information Section 3; Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). Comprehensive control experiments (Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14; Supplementary Figs. 9–11 and 20–22) verify that this transition and the integer doping are intrinsic, excluding artefacts such as contamination. We emphasize that the integer doping is a direct observation requiring no fitting or registration procedure. As is well established for graphene superlattices5,6,7, the neutrality point–secondary Dirac point separation is fixed at four electrons per moiré unit cell. In Fig. 2c, the post-transition neutrality point (red) falls precisely at the midpoint between the pre-transition neutrality point and the secondary Dirac point (blue) and hence corresponds to exactly two electrons per moiré unit cell, as highlighted by the equally spaced ruler.

According to recent reports, note that for the dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c), the gate voltage was applied simultaneously through top and bottom gates along the D = 0 line30 (dashed line in Fig. 3a). The switching depends only on the total carrier concentration and not on the displacement field (Supplementary Information Section 8; Supplementary Fig. 14). This mechanism fundamentally differs from recently reported two-dimensional ferroelectric systems, in which transitions occur through external electric-field-induced polarization changes26,31,32.

According to recent reports, to investigate the transition dynamics and reproducibility, we conducted a series of Vtg–Vbg mappings and repeated switching tests (Rxx in Fig. 3; Rxy in Supplementary Fig. 24). Figure 3a–c reveals several Dirac points separated by intervals of four electrons per moiré plaquette5,6,7, marked with blue (before transition) or red (after transition) lines or arrows.

It has been revealed that the phase transition occurs at Vtg = +3.9 V, Vbg = +5.3 V corresponding to ntotal = 3.75 × 1012 cm−2 along the D = 0 line in Fig. 3a. Following the transition, all features shift by two electrons per moiré plaquette. This shift throughout the entire superlattice spectrum clearly indicates that the moiré period is unchanged. The recovery occurs at Vtg = −5.0 V, Vbg = −6.9 V (corresponding to −4.85 × 1012 cm−2), also along the D = 0 line, restoring the entire gate dependence (Fig. 3b). Comparing Fig. 3c with Fig. 3a indicates that different Vtg–Vbg ranges and sweep protocols do not affect the transition characteristics: it occurs at identical gate points, as a single discrete event at the critical voltage rather than a continuous evolution.

Figure 3d illustrates the transition dynamics through sequential measurements (swp1–swp8), with dashed lines at +5.3 V and −6.9 V marking the critical voltages for the forward and reverse transitions, respectively. Below the critical voltage, no transition occurs (swp1–swp2); on reaching it, the transition happens (swp3–swp4), at a critical voltage independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15; Supplementary Fig. 23). Similar behaviour is observed for the reverse transition (steps swp4–swp7). Figure 3f,g shows zoomed-in views around the critical voltages for both the forward and reverse transitions. At the moment of transition, the resistance jumps from one state to another without any intermediate states, consistent with the abrupt translation of features observed in Vtg–Vbg mappings of Fig. 3a–c. Once the transition is induced, further increasing the gate voltage yields no continuous effect, indicating a saturation mechanism defined by the moiré unit cell capacity rather than the strength of the applied field. This behaviour differs markedly from that of ferroelectrics, for which polarization scales continuously with the applied field. The switching is fully reproducible: 100 consecutive cycles yield curves that overlap precisely (Fig. 3d, top). All behaviours discussed above support that the observed phase transition is a first-order-like transition (further information in Supplementary Information Section 43).

Notably, the transition can also be controlled by the magnetic field. Mapping the transition from 13 T down to 0 T (Fig. 3e) shows that the transition is suppressed at high field, even for gate voltages far exceeding the critical value, and reappears at exactly the same critical voltage once the field drops below Bcrit = 3.8 T. The origin of this suppression remains to be established; we note, however, that the magnetic length at critical field \(\sqrt{\hbar /e{B}_{{\rm{crit}}}}\approx 13.4\,{\rm{nm}}\) is comparable with the moiré period for this sample of 13.8 nm.

According to recent reports, in Fig. 3h, correlating Rxx with Rxy gives further information for theoretical analysis: the Hall-resistivity zero crossing (zero free carrier density nfree) occurs at a gate-induced density of two holes per moiré unit cell, the difference being compensated by localized electrons nloc.

To identify the origin of the phase transition, we consider the balance between elastic (strain) and van der Waals forces5,6, which can be modified through Coulomb interactions introduced by gate charging the graphene layer.

Sources indicate that using high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), we calculated the adhesion-energy distribution across the non-relaxed moiré plaquette, assuming perfect alignment of hBN on both sides, for the AB (Fig. 4a) and AA (Fig. 4b) relative configurations of the two hBN crystals (Supplementary Information Section 22; Supplementary Figs. 33–35). The relative energy of the two configurations can be compared by averaging the van der Waals potential over the entire moiré unit cell, as illustrated in Fig. 4c. The AB structure exhibits lower energy under neutral charging conditions (Fig. 4c–e). However, by assigning a negative charge on graphene above a certain threshold (corresponding to positive gate voltage applied) the AA configuration becomes more energetically favourable than AB (Fig. 4c,f,g), resulting in a structural phase transition from AB to AA.
