For a massive relativistic field, the transition from the low-energy quadratic dispersion to the higher-energy linear dispersion is set by the reduced Compton wavelength ƛ = ħ/(m*c), which here corresponds to the magnetic (Rabi) healing length \({\xi }_{{\rm{M}}}=\sqrt{\hbar /(2m\varOmega )}\). Our ability to tune \({\mu }_{{\rm{s}}}/(\hbar \varOmega )={({\xi }_{{\rm{M}}}/{\xi }_{{\rm{s}}})}^{2}\gg 1\) gives us a k range where the relativistic nature of the massive dispersion is key.

It has been revealed that we now turn to exploring the non-perturbative sine-Gordon dynamics, by initializing the system at a large global phase displacement ϕ0 (Fig. 5a).

a, We study the dynamics following a large initial phase displacement ϕ0. For ∣ϕ0∣ < π, the plasma-oscillation period is ϕ0-dependent owing to the concavity of U(ϕ). For ϕ0 = π, different regions of the system may eventually settle to different potential minima, which results in domain walls across which ϕ winds by 2π. b, Large-amplitude oscillations. Left: for different ϕ0, the system takes different time, τ, to return to ϕ = 0. Solid lines show sinusoidal fits; for large ϕ0, the oscillation is visibly anharmonic. Each data point is based on five independent experimental runs, and the error bars show the s.e.m. Right: τ/τ0 versus ϕ0; here τ0 = π/(2ωp) is the ϕ0-independent perturbative result. The solid line is the prediction based on the pendulum model. The errors in τ correspond to half of the spacing between the sampled t values. Here, Z0 = 0.31, Ω/(2π) = 74 Hz and μs/(ħΩ) ≈ 11. c,d, Domain walls. The system is prepared at ϕ ≈ π at t = 0, and allowed to relax for 10 ms, corresponding to approximately 7τ0; here Z0 = 0.53, Ω/(2π) = 22 Hz and μs/(ħΩ) ≈ 39. Scale bar, 20 μm. In c, we show examples of domain walls seen in n+ and n− images, where they appear as, respectively, low- and high-density lines; each image shows an independent realization. In d, we show phase maps that reveal the 2π phase winding at domain walls. We interfere the two spin states using a pair of Raman–Bragg laser beams with wavevectors q1,2, and the imaged density distribution, nRB, shows modulations \(\propto \cos ({\bf{q}}\cdot {\bf{r}}+\phi )\), where q = q1 − q2 and r = (x, y). From such fringe patterns we reconstruct the phase maps shown in the bottom panels (see text for details).

For ∣ϕ0∣ < π, we observe the anharmonic nature of the sine-Gordon potential, \(U(\phi )\propto -\cos (\phi )\), by measuring the time, τ, it takes the system to return from ϕ0 to ϕ = 0 (Fig. 5b). Here, we extract \(\phi =\arctan (Y/X)\), where Y and X are the separately measured projections of the global Bloch vector. In the perturbative regime, U(ϕ) is approximately harmonic and τ ≈ π/(2ωp) is independent of ϕ0. However, as ϕ0 → π, the concavity of U becomes increasingly relevant and τ grows, in analogy with a mechanical pendulum with a large initial angular displacement (solid line in Fig. 5b, right). At longer times these oscillations damp out, and this damping is accompanied by an emergence of spatial structures corresponding to k > 0 excitations (Extended Data Fig. 2).

It has been revealed that for ϕ0 = π, different regions of the system may settle into different potential minima, leading to the formation of domain walls across which ϕ rapidly winds by 2π. We observe such walls in most experimental realizations, with their spatial patterns varying randomly shot to shot (Fig. 5c,d).

In the images of n+ and n− (Fig. 5c), the walls appear as lines of low and high density, respectively. Here we show images from different experimental realizations, but note that if we image both n+ and n− in the same experimental run, we see that they are complementary (Extended Data Fig. 3).

Recent findings suggest that in Fig. 5d, we explicitly demonstrate the 2π phase winding across the domain walls. Here, just before imaging the \(|\uparrow \rangle \) component, we perform a fast (approximately 6 μs) π/2 spin rotation using a resonant two-photon Raman–Bragg coupling (see cartoon) instead of a radio-frequency field. Compared with the radio-frequency field that has a spatially uniform phase across the cloud, the Raman–Bragg coupling leads to a complex Ω with a spatially varying phase q ⋅ r; here r = (x, y) and q = q1 − q2, where q1,2 are the wavevectors of the two laser beams. In the Bloch-sphere picture, the Raman–Bragg Rabi vector always lies in the equatorial plane, but its orientation varies along the direction defined by q. Consequently, the imaged density nRB(x, y) demonstrates modulations \(\propto \cos ({\bf{q}}\cdot {\bf{r}}+\phi )\). For a spatially uniform ϕ, this is a pattern of straight parallel fringes with period 2π/q ≈ 2.51 μm, whereas spatial variations of ϕ(x, y) lead to fringe deformations. In particular, a domain wall perpendicular to q changes the fringe spacing, whereas a wall parallel to q shifts the fringe phase by 2π. In Fig. 5d, we show both  the straight fringes observed at t = 0 ms and two examples of domain walls observed after 10 ms of relaxation; the bottom panels show the reconstructed phase maps (see Extended Data Fig. 4 for more details).

Recent findings suggest that the characteristic width, w, of an equilibrium domain wall is set by the competition between the potential energy per unit length, ∝ ħΩ ⋅ nw, and the corresponding kinetic energy, ∝ ħ2/(2mw2) ⋅ nw. Similarly to the oscillator length in a quantum harmonic oscillator, this competition gives w = ƛ = \({\xi }_{{\rm{M}}}=\sqrt{\hbar /(2m\varOmega )}\).

Recent findings suggest that in Fig. 6a, we extract the domain-wall widths from both the n± images and the phase maps. In all cases, one-dimensional cuts perpendicular to the walls are fitted well by the theoretically predicted10 forms n±(z) = n0 ± n1sech2(z/w) and ϕ(z) = 4arctan[exp(z/w)]; here, z is the coordinate perpendicular to a wall centred at z = 0, and n0, n1 and w are fit parameters. The extracted values of w have a wide distribution (see histograms), probably because our domain walls are excited, but the three mean values are (within one standard deviation) consistent with each other and with the theoretically predicted w, indicated on the histograms by the dashed lines; it is noted that here we include an 8% correction to the predicted w due to our non-zero Z0 (Methods).

a, For the experimental protocol as in Fig. 5, we extract the wall widths, w, from n+ and n− images, such as shown in Fig. 5c, and the phase maps, such as shown in Fig. 5d. We fit cuts perpendicular to the walls to the theoretically expected profiles (solid lines, see text). The histograms show width distributions based on >100 experimental images, and the dashed lines indicate the theoretically predicted w. b, The effect of changing Ω on the domain-wall width. Here the experimental protocol is the same, except that for the last 2 ms of relaxation we jump Ω/(2π) from 22 Hz to either 10 Hz or 45 Hz. The representative n+ images show an increase of the wall widths in the former case and decrease in the latter. Scale bar, 20 μm. The summary of the extracted mean widths is consistent with the expected trend \(w\propto 1/\sqrt{\varOmega }\). The dashed line demonstrates the theoretically predicted w, including an 8% correction due to our non-zero Z0 (Methods). The solid line shows the same trend with systematically 15% lower values. The error bars show the standard deviations of the w distributions. The different symbols corresponding to the same Ω are slightly offset horizontally for clarity.

Industry observers note that finally, in Fig. 6b, we show that the characteristic wall width responds to changes in Ω. Here we initiate the system dynamics as in Fig. 5c, but quench Ω either down or up for the last 2 ms of relaxation. In the representative n+ images, one can see the systematic change in the wall widths, and the widths extracted as in Fig. 6a are consistent with the expected trend \(w\propto 1/\sqrt{\varOmega }\).

To conclude, we have established a versatile analogue simulator for self-interacting relativistic quantum fields with a tunable mass in 2 + 1 dimensions, and observed non-perturbative phenomena that point the way to many future studies. The damping of the global ϕ oscillations, accompanied by an emergence of spatial structures (k > 0 excitations), is expected to be analogous to cosmological preheating and reheating11,12. The π phase jump that places the field at the top of the sine-Gordon potential initiates dynamics associated with a quench through a discrete symmetry-breaking phase transition (with the energy minima changing from ϕ = π to ϕ = 0 and 2π). Generalizing the π phase jump to a ramp of Ω from a positive to a negative value, one can study the associated Kibble–Zurek mechanism50, linked to the formation of topological defects such as cosmic strings and domain walls13,14. Studies of domain-wall networks could provide insights into cosmological dark-matter production in axion scenarios51,52 and gravitational-wave signals in a broad family of particle-physics models53. In this context, a particularly interesting possibility is to use vector light shifts to deterministically imprint specific initial domain-wall configurations and study their subsequent dynamics, including their relaxation and decay54,55. Finally, using Floquet engineering to stabilize the system at ϕ = π would enable studies of false-vacuum decay15,16,41,42 in a relativistic, cosmologically relevant setting17,18,19.

Our experiments were performed in a uniform two-dimensional optical box trap formed by repulsive 532-nm light. The two-dimensional confinement was provided by an accordion lattice with trapping frequency ωz/(2π) ≈ 1 kHz, generated holographically56 with a digital micro-mirror device. The in-plane confinement was provided by a square box directly projected from another digital micro-mirror device through a high-resolution microscope (numerical aperture 0.7). The box size was approximately 50 μm × 50 μm for Fig. 1c, and 30 μm × 30 μm for the rest of the experiments.

The radio-frequency field that couples the two hyperfine states was derived from a vector signal generator (Keysight N5172B). Using in-phase and quadrature modulation, we independently and simultaneously controlled the amplitude, phase and frequency of the radio-frequency field; to prevent carrier feed-through from contaminating the signal, we used a 200-kHz baseband offset. This allowed us to dynamically attenuate the radio-frequency power by >60 dB, and realize Ω/(2π) ≲ 10Hz while retaining the ability to perform fast π/2 rotation at Ω/(2π) > 10kHz. The calibration error for Ω was ≲1% (standard deviation).

It has been revealed that to stabilize the magnetic field B, we first regulated the current through our coils using a feedback loop with a bandwidth >1 kHz and then cancelled the residual 50-Hz mains oscillations using feedforward. This cancelled most of the high-frequency noise from the power supply. To counter slow thermal drifts, we periodically (approximately once per minute) calibrated the field using partial Landau–Zener transfers. On the basis of Zerr from the calibration data, we estimated the residual field variations to be about 150 μG (root mean square).

According to recent reports, in the main text we give the simpler and more intuitive approximate equations that assume Z0 = 0. For all expressions in the main text other than equations (2) and (3), for which the exact forms can be obtained from equations (9) and (11), the corrections due to non-zero Z0 can be incorporated by simply replacing Ω by Ω′ and μs by \({\mu }_{{\rm{s}}}^{{\prime} }\). For our experiments, these corrections are usually negligible (compared with the statistical errors), as we illustrate in Fig. 3c by plotting both the predictions that take into account the Z0 corrections (dotted lines) and the approximate predictions that assume Z0 = 0 (solid lines). For Figs. 4 and 5, the corrections are similarly negligible and for simplicity we ignore them, using only the simpler theory given in the main text. The only perceptible correction, which we do include when comparing the data with theory, is in Fig. 6, where, for Z0 = 0.53, the expected wall width \(w=\sqrt{\hbar /(2m{\varOmega }^{{\prime} })}\) is approximately 8% smaller than \(\sqrt{\hbar /(2m\varOmega )}\).

In Extended Data Fig. 1, we also examine the range of k values for which the dispersion of our spin modes, ωs(k) in equation (5), mimics well the relativistic dispersion ωr(k) in equation (6). As long as k < 1/ξs, the difference between ωs and ωr is ≲20% even for Ω = 0, and it reduces with increasing Ω.

Most importantly, the domain walls we observe in Figs. 5 and 6 are deep in the long-wavelength, relativistic regime. For these walls, the relevant k modes are k ≲ 1/w, and even for our largest Ω in Fig. 6, 1/w is still smaller than the smallest 1/ξM (purple dashed line) shown in Extended Data Fig. 1. In this k range, ωs(k) and ωr(k) are essentially identical.

In Extended Data Fig. 2, we illustrate how the large-amplitude plasma oscillations, such as shown in Fig. 5b, damp at long times. This damping is accompanied by emergence of spatial structures corresponding to a transfer of energy from k = 0 to higher-k modes; qualitatively, this is what is expected in models of cosmological preheating and reheating11,12.

In Extended Data Fig. 3, we create domain walls as in Fig. 5c, and take consecutive images of n+ and n− in the same experimental run, which shows that the two density distributions are complementary.

In a recent development, from our nRB(x, y) images, we extract ϕtot = q ⋅ r + ϕ using a convolutional neural network59, trained on synthetic data that mimic the experimental images. The network generates quadrature maps I(x, y) and Q(x, y) that approximate, respectively, \(\cos [{\phi }_{{\rm{tot}}}(x,y)]\) and \(\sin [{\phi }_{{\rm{tot}}}(x,y)]\), and we extract ϕtot(x, y) as the phase of I(x, y) + iQ(x, y).

In Extended Data Fig. 4, we illustrate the fidelity of this extraction for two examples shown in Fig. 5d and two additional ones from the same dataset. Left to right, we show: (1) the nRB images, (2) the reconstructed \([1+\cos ({\phi }_{{\rm{tot}}})]/2\), which is essentially the de-noised version of the fringes seen in nRB, (3) the contours tracing the maxima of the reconstructed fringes, (4) the overlaying of these contours on the original images, and (5) the extracted ϕ(x, y).

According to recent reports, we obtain ϕ(x, y) from ϕtot(x, y) by subtracting the independently calibrated carrier phase q ⋅ r, but note that, because the relative phase between the Raman–Bragg beams and the radio-frequency coupling is random, our measurement determines ϕ(x, y) only up to a global offset. We fix this offset such that ⟨eiϕ⟩ is real and negative for t = 0 ms (as ϕ is jumped to π), and real and positive for t = 10 ms (appropriate for relaxation to ϕ = 0 (mod 2π), as observed in the n± images).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool would have a €23m offer accepted if they make it. The Reds are weighing up a deal that could help transform their season.

Do Liverpool need a new left-back? Really, the question is 'when' - everyone expects Kostas Tsimikas to leave the club at the end of the season when his contract expires.

So it's a matter of what kind of replacement Liverpool opt for. Do they simply want to find a backup player to Milos Kerkez? Or is it a chance to replace him?

Sources indicate that there are other possibilities here, too. Liverpool could take advantage of the squad space to find a versatile player who fills a few roles. Or perhaps they want an experienced player who can fit into the leadership group.

In a recent development, then there's the homegrown question. Liverpool could make things easier for themselves by adding a couple of homegrown players and here's a good opportunity to add one. Should they wish.

Or maybe, above all, they just want an elite left-back who could potentially replace Kerkez as first-choice.

Archie Brown is wanted - and has a clauseTurkish outlet Takvim reports that Liverpool are in the running for Fenerbahçe left-back Archie Brown. The 24-year-old is wanted by several Premier League clubs and for good reason - he's homegrown. Brown made a significant impact against Liverpool this season, of course, as he both scored and assisted in his side's 3-2 win over the Reds. It's something that's catapulted Brown into the spotlight as one to watch, particularly for Premier League sides.

Industry observers note that turkish outlet Takvim reports that Liverpool are in the running for Fenerbahçe left-back Archie Brown. The 24-year-old is wanted by several Premier League clubs and for good reason - he's homegrown.

Brown made a significant impact against Liverpool this season, of course, as he both scored and assisted in his side's 3-2 win over the Reds. It's something that's catapulted Brown into the spotlight as one to watch, particularly for Premier League sides.

The interest is significant enough that we can't imagine the player moves anywhere where he isn't first choice. He's set to have his pick of clubs, too, as a release clause in his contract guarantees that the fee won't get out of hand.

Sources indicate that that price is €23m, which is arguably a complete steal for a UEFA Champions League-level left-back right now. Especially one who's English.

Industry observers note that we expect Brown to be one of Liverpool's most-wanted in 2027 and there's half a chance that they get the deal done in January. After all, that clause won't be around forever - someone is going to trigger it sooner or later. Another club, then, could force the Reds' hand by making a winter offer.

Absolutely, then, this is one to watch.

#48902. The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1171 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

Industry observers note that the plate and the photos are on show at the latest exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, says exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Recent findings suggest that alongside Picasso, a surprising number of key artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

According to recent reports, however, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

Recent findings suggest that the dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked significant and dangerous.".

The endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian says. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a new image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

Sources indicate that the designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

Still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

Industry observers note that but altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

Industry observers note that the feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

According to recent reports, "It's really crazy," she says, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026.

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'.

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness.

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list.

Joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an important part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

According to recent reports, post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences.

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

It has been revealed that however, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

According to recent reports, there were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010).

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” said Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

Recent findings suggest that “I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a massive difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”.

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”.

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”.

It has been revealed that palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

In a recent development, palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

According to recent reports, bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January aims

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (477 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it.
  • It has been revealed that juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in upcoming capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November.
  • Part of the money is already committed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

It has been revealed that juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in upcoming capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

According to recent reports, the squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

Recent findings suggest that the assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

In a recent development, that agreement was unveiled on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

It has been revealed that for supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how rapidly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 20:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:00.

It has been revealed that coventry City vs. Crystal Palace is the sort of match that will keep Frank Lampard's men in the Premier League if they can prevail, an ex-Sky Blues striker has told Sports Mole.

Coventry host Crystal Palace in the Eagles' first fixture under new head coach Thomas Frank, who takes over from Pierre Sage with the Eagles languishing at the bottom of the Premier League table.

The hosts, meanwhile, are three places and two points better off in the relative safety of 17th spot, having taken nine points from their opening 10 games of their first top-flight season in 25 years.

Two of Coventry's three league triumphs this season have come at the CBS Arena, both against bottom-half rivals in Newcastle United and Sunderland, although Fulham and Hull City have also got the better of them in front of their own fans.

Former Coventry striker Mark Hateley - who scored 27 goals in a century of appearances for the Sky Blues - is fearing a upcoming manager bounce for Palace, but warned his old club that this type of match could dictate their survival chances.

Industry observers note that “You always get that bounce from a new manager," Hateley mentioned. "You get it for one, two, three games, and then it starts to wear off. Thomas Frank is a proven tactician who sees things very rapidly within a team.

“Palace still have a really decent side with decent players, so I think he'll be in and about it quickly, and you'll see a style of play that he gets from what he sees in that group of players. Whether it lasts all the way through, I don't know, but I think he'll fix Palace into a side that will be OK.

According to recent reports, “Coventry are the other side. They've got to survive this year and build for the next two years: survival, survival, survival. Palace will know how to do it; they've got good enough players. But these are the games Coventry should be looking to win. These are the games that keep you in the league.”.

Saturday's match will mark the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal Palace since the 2011-12 Championship season, when the Sky Blues lost 2-1 away before holding the Eagles to a 1-1 draw at home.

Coventry earned their most recent victory against Crystal Palace shortly beforehand, prevailing 2-1 in February 2011 thanks to goals from Richard Wood and Marlon King.

Taking data across all competitions from Lampard's Coventry tenure so far and Frank's lengthy spell at Brentford from 2018 to 2025, the statistics somewhat favour the Chelsea legend.

Indeed, Lampard boasts more points per game, more goals scored per match and fewer goals conceded per match, while also winning one trophy in the form of the Championship.

However, those numbers must certainly be taken with a pinch of salt given Frank's substantially longer spell at Brentford, and the Dane's four full seasons in the top flight after winning promotion with the Bees.

It has been revealed that lampard's Coventry have nevertheless shown promising signs after he also succeeded in keeping Everton afloat in the top flight, though, so Saturday's edition of Frank vs. Frank is a challenging one to call.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

Manchester United have reportedly made a key decision on Harry Amass ahead of the January transfer window, as they look to resolve ongoing uncertainty at left-back.

The 19-year-old academy graduate had been linked with a permanent departure from Old Trafford during the summer. However, United now appear ready to protect his future by extending his contract, while leaving open the possibility of another loan move.

With injuries affecting the club’s senior defensive options, Amass’ situation could become increasingly important in the coming months.

According to the Evening Standard, Manchester United are preparing to trigger a 12-month extension clause in Amass’ existing contract.

The decision would give the club greater control over the defender’s future and prevent him from approaching the end of his deal without a resolution.

Amass attracted interest from Burnley during the summer after spending time on loan with Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City. A permanent exit appeared possible, but United ultimately retained the youngster.

The club’s latest reported decision suggests they are not ready to lose control of a player who remains a promising defensive prospect.

United’s situation at left-back has been complicated by fitness concerns involving Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

It has been revealed that shaw has struggled with injuries throughout his career, while Dorgu has provided an alternative option when available. Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can also cover the position, although both are more naturally suited to right-back.

These challenges could influence whether Amass stays at Old Trafford or is allowed to leave on loan in January.

Regular first-team football would be valuable for the young defender’s development, but United may be reluctant to weaken their depth while senior players remain unavailable.

A temporary move remains a possibility if United believe Amass would benefit from more regular playing time elsewhere.

His previous loan spells offered opportunities to gain senior experience, although an injury interrupted his time at Norwich City last season.

According to recent reports, united must now balance his development against their immediate need for defensive cover. Extending his contract would give the club additional flexibility to make that decision without risking his longer-term value.

The situation could also affect United’s plans for recruiting another left-back, particularly if the club decide they need a more established option.

United’s reported decision to extend Amass’ contract would provide greater security over his future, but it does not guarantee that he will remain in the first-team squad for the rest of the season.

Recent findings suggest that A January loan could still make sense if Shaw and Dorgu are fit enough to provide cover. If injuries continue, however, Amass may have an opportunity to establish himself at Old Trafford.

Juventus won 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar on a night when Teun Koopmeiners faced his old club, even though the hosts dominated the expected-goals count. The result strengthens their league-phase position ahead of Sunday's Serie A trip to Fiorentina.

Recent findings suggest that the trip to Alkmaar returned Teun Koopmeiners to his former club. His brother Peer was in the AZ side that Juventus then held off. UEFA picked out the family meeting in its matchday 4 round-up.

Koopmeiners opened the scoring in the 19th minute from a Kolo Muani pass. Kolo Muani doubled the lead in the 37th minute, with Nick Woltemade credited with the assist, and Juventus led 2-0 at half-time. Kolo Muani earned a rating of 8.61 from the data provider, with Koopmeiners on 8.2.

Recent findings suggest that AZ pulled one back in the 88th minute. Mexx Meerdink scored from an Elijah Dijkstra assist. The hosts could not find an equaliser in the remaining minutes.

The home side had 56% of possession. They completed 523 passes to Juventus’s 378. Eleven of AZ’s attempts were blocked, against three of Juventus’s.

According to recent reports, both teams put three shots on target. Vicario made two saves for Juventus. AZ’s expected goals total points to the chances the hosts created without converting them.

It has been revealed that the figures are consistent with a Juventus side defending a first-half lead. Spalletti’s team committed 20 fouls to AZ’s 13. Andrea Cambiaso, Jeff Ekhator and Juan Cabal were booked for Juventus. Wesley Hoedt was the only AZ player shown a yellow card. Damian Sylwestrzak refereed the match.

The victory was Spalletti’s second in a row in all competitions, following the league win over Napoli. It came after a run that included a 0-2 defeat to Genoa and a 0-3 loss to Lazio. Koopmeiners now has four goals for Juventus in all competitions in 2026, one more than the three he scored for the club in 2025, Sky Sport Italia noted.

Sources indicate that for AZ, the result was a third straight defeat in all competitions. Losses to Ajax and Twente came before Thursday’s game.

This season’s league phase has 36 clubs, and each plays eight different opponents. It ends on Thursday 28 January 2027. Juventus host Omonia Nicosia on 26 November at 21:00 CET, while AZ travel to Sparta Praha. Juventus then visit Hapoel Beer-Sheva on 10 December and Ferencváros on 21 January 2027, both at 18:45 CET. They finish at home to Real Sociedad on 28 January 2027 at 21:00 CET.

Sources indicate that serie A comes first. Juventus travel to Fiorentina for matchday 11 on Sunday 8 November, with kick-off at 20:45. AZ host Groningen in the Eredivisie on the same day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 20:16, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:18.

Both Racing de Santander and Real Sociedad will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in Spain's top flight when they lock horns on Sunday afternoon.

Real Sociedad lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 49 wins to 34, while the Basque outfit have triumphed in the last three meetings.

Racing have a record of four wins, two draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 14 points leaving them in 10th spot in the La Liga table.

Jose Alberto's side entered the November international break off the back of a 2-1 victory over Malaga, and they have actually won three of their last four games in all competitions.

The Green and Whites are the reigning Segunda Division champions, securing a return to this level courtesy of their excellent second-tier campaign in 2025-26, and their main aim for this season will be to consolidate back in the top flight.

Racing have not managed to overcome Real Sociedad since March 2011, while they have just one victory over the Basque side since January 2007.

The Green and Whites have been impressive on home soil this season, picking up 11 points from their six matches in front of their own supporters.

Real Sociedad, meanwhile, boast a record of seven wins, one draw and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 22 points leaving them fifth in the table.

The Basque outfit are only four points off fourth-placed Real Betis, and an excellent run of form in Spain's top flight has seen them win five of their last six matches.

La Real are also playing in the Europa League this season, picking up five points from their four matches to sit down in 20th position in the league stage.

Real Sociedad's last league match ended in a 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano before the November international break, and they will have their eyes on another three points here before heading to England next week to tackle Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

Real Sociedad form (all competitions):.

Racing need to make late checks on Alvaro Mantilla and Andres Martin, but the hosts are otherwise in strong shape for their clash with Real Sociedad.

Yassir Zabiri has been in impressive form this season, scoring nine goals in 12 appearances, and the number 21 will continue through the middle for the hosts.

There is also expected to be a spot in the side for Ivan Martin.

As for Real Sociedad, Alvaro Odriozola remains unavailable for selection due to a knee injury, while Ander Barrenetxea is a major doubt due to a hamstring injury.

Mikel Oyarzabal missed the team's final match ahead of the November international break through illness, but the attacker has since returned for Spain, and it is possible that he could start in a wide area on Sunday due to the form of Orri Oskarsson.

The 22-year-old, who is being linked with a move to Manchester United, has scored four times in 10 league appearances this season, including the winner against Rayo Vallecano last time out, and he is again set to feature in the XI.

Racing de Santander possible starting lineup:.

Agirrezabala; Ramon, Felipe, Belocian, Salinas; I Martin, Prati; Luque, Canales, Vicente; Zabiri.

Real Sociedad possible starting lineup:.

Remiro; Aramburu, Martin, Zubeldia, Munoz; Turrientes, Soler; Kubo, Sucic, Oyarzabal; Oskarsson.

Real Sociedad have lost three of their six away league matches this season, while Racing have been solid at home, so we are struggling to back a victory for the visitors and have instead settled on a low-scoring draw.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

According to recent reports, “Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a significant asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”.

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”.

In a recent development, for Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be vital. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

It has been revealed that rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

Industry observers note that the comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

In a recent development, nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

Sparta Rotterdam vs AZ Alkmaar - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 20:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:58.
  • A struggling Sparta Rotterdam outfit will set out in search of a return to winning ways in Sunday’s Eredivisie clash against AZ Alkmaar at Het Kasteel.
  • The visitors, meanwhile, travel to Rotterdam aiming for back-to-back wins for the first time since September, having snapped a three-game losing streak just before the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 20:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:58.

A struggling Sparta Rotterdam outfit will set out in search of a return to winning ways in Sunday’s Eredivisie clash against AZ Alkmaar at Het Kasteel.

The visitors, meanwhile, travel to Rotterdam aiming for back-to-back wins for the first time since September, having snapped a three-game losing streak just before the international break.

AZ Alkmaar started the season with six wins and a draw from their opening seven Eredivisie matches, looking like the team to beat, but a 2-0 defeat to Feyenoord after the September break sparked a four-game winless run (D1, L3).

In arguably the game of the season so far, Leeroy Echteld’s men scored three times in the final 30 minutes of their most recent clash against Groningen to secure a 4-3 victory and keep themselves within three points of PSV Eindhoven at the top of the Eredivisie table.

De Kaasboeren have failed to win any of their league matches immediately preceding a Europa League group-stage fixture so far, and with a trip to Sparta Prague to follow this weekend, they will be eager to buck that trend of faltering domestically before continental duties.

AZ won both league meetings with Sparta last season, making it four wins from the last six encounters (D1, L1). Sunday’s visitors are also unbeaten in their last six trips to Het Kasteel, averaging two goals per game in that stretch.

However, AZ have struggled away from home recently, collecting just one point from the last nine available on their travels, which came in a 2-2 draw at Cambuur courtesy of a Mexx Merdink penalty seven minutes from time.

While not their heaviest, Sparta’s 3-1 defeat to newly-promoted ADO Den Haag was arguably their most disappointing loss of the 2026-27 season so far, especially given the momentum they carried into the clash after a thrilling 3-2 triumph over Groningen.

Rogier Meijer has now lost more than half of his 13 matches since taking charge in July, and pressure is beginning to mount on the 45-year-old.

Nevertheless, his experience at this level - having recently surpassed 200 matches as a manager in Dutch football - suggests he will be given time to turn things around.

Starting this weekend’s clash just two points clear of the drop zone, De Rood-Witte Gladiatoren risk ending matchday 13 inside the relegation places - a significant fall from grace for a side tipped to compete for Europe at the start of the campaign.

Only Utrecht and Willem II have conceded more goals than Sparta’s 29, and they are also one of five teams without a clean sheet, leaving little mystery about their biggest shortcoming this season.

Averaging 1.8 goals per game so far, Sunday’s hosts have fared reasonably well in attack, but an overreliance on Milan Zonneveld, who has been directly involved in nine of their 21 goals, can sometimes prove detrimental.

#48885. Breaking: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

Breaking: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1723 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a new £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.

I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular new 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.

Interestingly, the meeting came in a week when Jacobo Solis, the influential Public Investment Fund executive and club director who is rarely seen in the city, was also present. The Spaniard’s involvement is viewed as extremely significant by those close to the project, and we understand an announcement on the club’s stadium looks is now ‘very close’.

The high-level meeting with Goldman Sachs is a major indication the club's board will recommend the development of a new stadium rather than redeveloping St James’, and I understand the former is currently the preference.

There has been significant outlay on various surveys around Leazes Park in recent months. I reported in April how the presence of bats in the area was one environmental complication they had to overcome. The club has since undertaken extensive work around animal and plant life.

The alternative remains a St James’ expansion, taking the capacity to 60,000, but chief executive David Hopkinson and others among the top brass are well aware that only a new, multi-purpose home would allow Newcastle to compete financially with the world’s biggest clubs.

A secret meeting with representatives from Goldman Sachs is the strongest indication yet the club are preparing to leave St James' Park rather than redevelop it.

In a recent development, in April, Daily Mail Sport revealed an architect’s drawing of how the new, three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated.

Intends of the new stadium reveal an exterior that has been likened to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena.

The proposed funding model combines borrowing, owner investment and potentially outside investors, with the debt sitting with Newcastle rather than the ownership. That makes the involvement of Goldman Sachs particularly significant as the club look to turn their ambitious looks into a financially viable reality.

According to recent reports, sources have described the circular design of a new stadium, and in April we revealed an architect’s drawing of how the three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated, but the exterior has been likened to both Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena and Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium by those who have seen images and video.

Industry observers note that club sources say they are continuing to work on options and plans for a latest stadium. But the visit of Goldman Sachs – and the simultaneous presence of one of PIF's most influential figures – suggests that work behind the scenes is moving towards a decisive stage.

Having covered this story for several years, I now believe PIF will be asked to sign off on a upcoming stadium development ahead of an announcement in early 2027.

Dedic case closed - but he's told to bow out.

Amar Dedic has been given a rap on the knuckles and handed over his bow and arrows after the Newcastle defender’s ‘suspicious activity’ triggered a major police operation earlier this month.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed on November 5 that the Bosnian was at the centre of a search involving at least six patrol cars after he was spotted carrying the hunting weaponry at a Northumberland beauty spot.

A concerned 999 caller, believing there could be a threat to the public, reported seeing him and a friend walking with the equipment near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the Harlow Hill area, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were intercepted in a blaze of blue lights around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Newcastle United's Amar Dedic has had his bow and arrows taken away from him after causing a major incident earlier this month.

Recent findings suggest that in a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic and his friend. After lengthy discussions at the roadside, police were satisfied that Dedic was using the weaponry for recreational use, but their investigation remained open.

However, I can confirm the matter is now closed and the 24-year-old has been reminded of UK law by police and the club. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in this country.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson told me: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, November 4, we received a report of suspicious activity in the Harlow Hill area.

Sources indicate that ‘It was reported that two men had been witnessed in possession of bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road. Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

Industry observers note that 'At that time, it was understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Following a number of enquiries, this has now been confirmed. The two men have since forfeited the bow and arrows and words of advice have been given to the pair. The case has now been closed.’.

Dedic took the confusion in good spirit, posting a picture of Lord of the Rings character Legolas, known for his prowess with a bow and arrow, on his social media page.

Joelinton has not yet been ruled out of the Tyne-Wear derby, despite fears over a significant injury lay-off.

I revealed on November 4 that the Brazilian had suffered a fresh muscle strain and this was confirmed by Matthias Jaissle the following day. There has been a suggestion this week that the period out could extend towards Christmas, but sources have played down that possibility.

Industry observers note that I understand Joelinton is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures. This could still be too soon for the visit of Sunderland on December 6, but the noises around the midfielder have definitely been more optimistic in the past 24 hours. The 30-year-old is expected to be the only senior absentee from the squad that takes on Arsenal this weekend.

Joelinton (left) is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures.

According to recent reports, newcastle will NOT be signing Gambian triallists Omar Marong and Alieu Saine. I understand that, while the 16-year-olds have impressed during a two-week stay, club chiefs have decided that those already on the books are of greater potential.

They caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals.

It has been revealed that neither player could have signed permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle were keen to assess their potential. It is likely that players of a similar profile from Africa will arrive on trial in the future.

Arteta to meet old foe at St James'.

Both Jaissle and Mikel Arteta will walk suspension tightropes at St James’ Park on Saturday. The Newcastle and Arsenal bosses are on two bookings for the season – and a third means a one-game touchline ban.

Sources indicate that interestingly, the fourth official with whom Arteta clashed at Sunderland earlier this season will be on duty. Elliot Bell repeatedly warned Arteta not to step from his technical zone at the Stadium of Light.

According to recent reports, when the Spaniard infringed on Sunderland’s managerial area for a third time, referee John Brooks issued a yellow card. Arteta then appeared to sarcastically target Bell with a ‘just tick the box’ gesture.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is a booking away from a one-game touchline ban.

The 2023 match between Newcastle and Arsenal at St James' Park was settled by a controversial winner, with Joelinton accused of a push on Gabriel.

According to recent reports, in another twist, Stuart Attwell will be the VAR this weekend. He was the referee in charge when Newcastle beat Arsenal 1-0 three years ago. The controversial winning goal that night was scored by Anthony Gordon amid suspicion the ball had run out of play before Joe Willock crossed.

Joelinton was then accused by Arsenal of a push on defender Gabriel, while Gordon looked offside. All three incidents survived VAR checks and Attwell’s on-field decision stood.

Arteta was furious and branded the decision an ‘absolute disgrace’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arsenal subsequently issued an official statement backing his criticism and demanded improved refereeing standards. Arteta was charged by the FA over his comments but was eventually cleared.

However, the Premier League's independent Key Match Incidents panel ruled by a 4-1 majority that the goal had correctly been allowed to stand.

Finally, after James Trafford starred during England's 3-2 win in Spain this week, a brilliant match I was lucky enough to cover, one reader reached out to ask about an XI of players Newcastle have missed out on.

Newcastle's What Might Have Been XI (3-5-2): James Trafford; Abdukodir Khusanov, Tosin Adarabioyo, Marc Guehi; Ivan Fresneda, Johan Manzambi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, James Maddison, Victor Munoz; Joao Pedro, Hugo Ekitike.

  • Real Madrid's reported aims to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 20:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:01.

Real Madrid's reported aims to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.

Los Blancos are reportedly preparing to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option for the Como playmaker next summer, having watched his remarkable development under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, Madrid have decided to exercise the clause, which can only be triggered during the summer 2027 transfer window.

The 22-year-old has scored six goals and provided eight assists in 14 club appearances this season, establishing himself as one of the most influential attacking midfielders in Italian football.

However, Veron's latest assessment of Paz offers more than an extraordinary comparison with two of Argentina's greatest players.

The former Argentina international has also emphasised the importance of regular football in developing young talents, a consideration that could become significant if Paz returns to a Madrid squad already containing Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler.

Speaking in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, Veron reserved exceptional praise for Paz after the midfielder continued his impressive international development.

"Nico Paz has incredible talent. He is destined for great things," the former Manchester United midfielder noted. "The future belongs to him if he continues to behave like a professional, as he is doing.".

It has been revealed that veron then made a particularly striking comparison. "At 22, I have only seen Messi and a certain Diego Armando Maradona do certain things like that.".

It has been revealed that the 51-year-old was careful not to suggest that Paz was guaranteed to reach the extraordinary heights achieved by either legend. "I don't mean that he will reach those levels, but he has the qualities to attempt it," Veron explained.

What particularly impresses the former Chelsea midfielder is the confidence Paz displays when receiving possession under pressure.

Veron highlighted the youngster's ability to dictate the rhythm of attacks, move into dangerous positions and retain the trust of his teammates even when closely marked.

Rather than describing him solely as an individual talent, he identified Paz as the player around whom Como organise much of their attacking football.

Sources indicate that "Nico is a leader in the way he manages moves. He is the focal point of the game," Veron added.

Those qualities have become increasingly apparent under Fabregas, whose possession-based approach has allowed the Argentine to develop into a central figure.

In a recent development, paz has also carried his club form onto the international stage. He recently scored twice for Argentina against Costa Rica, further strengthening his credentials as one of the country's leading young talents following Messi's international retirement.

His performances have inevitably increased speculation surrounding his next move, with Madrid retaining a significant advantage over other potential suitors.

Paz left Madrid for Como in the summer of 2024, having made only eight senior appearances for the Spanish giants.

His move to Italy initially offered an opportunity to gain regular first-team experience, but the relationship between the two clubs has since become more complicated.

During the summer of 2026, Como reportedly paid an additional €60m to acquire full ownership of the player, while Madrid retained a final buy-back option worth €80m.

That clause is valid for the summer of 2027, meaning Madrid have a limited opportunity to bring their former academy player back on preferential terms.

COPE now reports that the Spanish giants intend to exercise that option, although the deal has not been officially completed.

As previously reported by Sports Mole, Madrid face an notable decision over Paz's future, particularly because of the attacking competition awaiting him at the Bernabeu.

Bellingham has established himself as a key figure in Madrid's midfield, while Guler has also become increasingly influential under Jose Mourinho.

Sources indicate that the club possesses several other attacking options, including Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Yan Diomande. Consequently, there is no guarantee that Paz would enjoy the same importance in Madrid's starting XI that he presently possesses at Como.

Veron's comments about another young Argentine, Franco Mastantuono, offer an interesting perspective on that challenge.

Discussing the youngster's development during his loan spell at Fiorentina, Veron argued that consistent opportunities were essential for establishing himself at the highest level.

Sources indicate that "Nico Paz became a leader at Como by playing," he explained. "I have never known a player who became a team leader by sitting on the bench.".

Industry observers note that veron was discussing the benefits of regular football rather than explicitly warning Paz against returning to Madrid. Nevertheless, his observations underline an important consideration for the Spanish club as it weighs up the midfielder's future.

Paz reportedly chose to remain at Como last summer because he wanted to continue developing through regular appearances, and his decision has been rewarded by an outstanding start to the newly introduced campaign.

Manchester United have also been linked with the Argentina international, although Madrid's contractual advantage places the Spanish giants in a stronger position.

Industry observers note that for Los Blancos, securing a player whose value has risen considerably could represent an attractive investment. For Paz, the sporting challenge would be to turn the promise recognised by Veron into an influential role at a club where competition for attacking positions is already fierce.

Manchester City are continuing to invest in young talent as they look to strengthen their squad for the future, with another exciting prospect emerging on their transfer radar.

Pep Guardiola’s side have reportedly moved into pole position for one of Borussia Dortmund’s most highly rated youngsters.

United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are right now considered the favourites to secure his signature.

With the teenager’s first-team opportunities limited in Germany, the Premier League champions could look to take advantage of the situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester City are the frontrunners to sign Albert after making a formal approach during the summer transfer window.

Recent findings suggest that the report claims City are prepared to offer the 17-year-old lucrative personal terms as they step up their pursuit. Their interest is serious, with the club previously prepared to meet a valuation in the region of €20 million (£16.7m).

Sources indicate that chelsea are also long-term admirers of the youngster and were reportedly willing to spend a similar amount last winter. Paris Saint-Germain previously made contact with Dortmund in 2025, while Arsenal and Liverpool have more recently been monitoring his situation.

However, City are currently viewed as being in the strongest position should Dortmund soften their stance.

Albert joined Borussia Dortmund from the LA Galaxy academy in 2024 and has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting young American talents in European football. He has already made Bundesliga appearances and earned senior international recognition with the United States.

Sources indicate that despite his potential, opportunities under Niko Kovac have been limited this season. That lack of regular first-team football has encouraged several clubs to monitor his development, although Dortmund remain determined to keep hold of their young attacker.

The Bundesliga side have reportedly rejected approaches, including loan enquiries, and continue to view Albert as an key part of their long-term plans. They are also preparing a contract extension offer, with his current agreement running until June 2027.

Sources indicate that there is another important factor for City. Premier League regulations prevent English clubs from signing Albert permanently until he turns 18 in May, meaning any potential transfer would be geared towards next summer rather than an immediate move.
